change_summary: PLOS ONE retracted this paper, whose title the notice repeats, because of concerns about peer review integrity and potential manipulation of the publication process. The notice says these concerns call into question the validity and provenance of the reported results, so the whole paper's findings cannot be relied on. The author either did not respond or could not be reached.
evaluation: Your Section 3 cites Dutta [14] as the main evidence for choosing an LSTM, quoting its 97.4% and 96.8% accuracy, and you decided not to run a model-selection study on that basis. Your Section 4 also starts from the LURL settings reported in that paper and does not plan to tune them. The retraction notice says concerns call the validity and provenance of the reported results into question, and it covers the whole paper, so both uses are touched. The impact is high, because the paper is your main evidence for the classifier choice and the source of your starting parameters.
recommendation: The editors retracted the article, and the concerns call into question the validity and provenance of the reported results. Your Section 4 starts from the LURL settings reported in that paper and does not plan to tune them. Raise this with your co-authors or supervisor before the pilot, since the settings depend on the retracted paper and editing the text won't fix that. Your Section 3 cites the paper as the main evidence for choosing an LSTM. Replace that citation with independent evidence, or run your own model comparison, and cite the retraction notice if you mention the paper at all.
